To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Latina/os are a growing, diverse population in the U.S.; (b) they are a population at high risk for developing mental health disorders; (c) they are a group that is under-served and under-treated in the health care system; and (d) they are a growing population in need of mental and behavioral health services, yet are under-served by the health care system.
Latina/os are a growing, underserved population in need of integrated care, and the current policies in place do not address the needs of this population.
the Latino community faces significant barriers to access and service utilization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of a model of culturally sensitive integrated care for Latina/os.
the need to improve access to care, and to improve the quality of care, and to ensure that the care is appropriate for the Latino population.
the need for policy and decision making that is culturally informed, and responsive to the unique needs of the Latino/a population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a great need for more culturally responsive policies that promote equity and access to mental health services for Latino populations.
the current system of care for Latinos is in need of major overhaul.
there is a need for more research, and that the research that does exist is often not used to inform practice, policy, or training.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are all walking on eggshells, but that we must work to make the eggs stronger and more resilient.
the Latino community is not walking on eggshells, but is committed to the work ahead.
we need to move from “walking on eggshells” to “commitment” in our policies and practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to move away from walking on eggshells to a commitment to culturally responsive care for Latina/os.
we are all in this together.
the mental health and health care system is not designed to meet the needs of Latino populations.
